title: Quiz: Trends in the Periodic Table

questions.stem: What happens to atomic radius as you go across a period from left to right?

options.text: It increases
It first increases then decreases
It decreases
It stays the same

questions.explanation: Atomic radius decreases across a period because the number of protons increases (stronger nuclear charge) while electrons are added to the same shell, pulling the electrons closer to the nucleus.

questions.stem: What happens to atomic radius as you go down a group?

options.text: It increases because additional electron shells are added
It decreases because of increasing nuclear charge
It depends on the specific group
It stays the same

questions.explanation: Atomic radius increases down a group because each element has an additional electron shell, making the atom physically larger despite the increasing nuclear charge.

options.text: The energy required to remove one electron from an atom
The energy needed to break a chemical bond
The energy needed to melt a substance
The energy released when an atom gains an electron

questions.explanation: Ionisation energy is the energy required to remove one electron from an atom in the gas phase. Higher ionisation energy means the electron is harder to remove.

questions.stem: How does ionisation energy change across a period from left to right?

options.text: It has no trend
It stays constant
It generally decreases
It generally increases

questions.explanation: Ionisation energy generally increases across a period because the increasing nuclear charge attracts the outer electrons more strongly, making them harder to remove.

questions.stem: Why does the reactivity of metals increase down a group?

options.text: The atoms have fewer electrons
The nuclear charge decreases
The outer electrons are further from the nucleus and easier to lose
The atoms become smaller

questions.explanation: Going down a group, the outer electrons are further from the nucleus with more shielding from inner shells. This makes them easier to lose, increasing the reactivity of metals.

questions.stem: Why does the reactivity of non-metals decrease down a group?

options.text: Non-metals become metals further down the group
The outer shell is further from the nucleus, making it harder to attract extra electrons
Non-metals become lighter down the group
Non-metals have fewer electrons down the group

questions.explanation: Non-metals react by gaining electrons. Going down the group, the outer shell is further from the nucleus with more shielding, so the atom attracts incoming electrons less strongly, reducing reactivity.

questions.stem: What is electronegativity, and how does it change across a period?

options.text: The ability to conduct electricity; it decreases across a period
The size of an atom; it increases across a period
The ability to attract bonding electrons; it generally increases across a period
The ability to lose electrons; it increases across a period

questions.explanation: Electronegativity is the ability of an atom to attract the bonding pair of electrons in a covalent bond. It generally increases across a period as nuclear charge increases and atomic radius decreases.
